content.text: Quick sanity check of the pure modules with Node:

I've fixed all six bugs and added the three features, but none of it has been run. My attempts to run Node for a syntax check and some quick tests were blocked by the permission prompt, so I checked the code by reading it only. Loading the page and clicking through the cases below would confirm it.

**Bugs**
1. **Monthly repeat (`js/recurring.js`)**: months that don't have the start day were being skipped. They now use their last day instead, so rent from Jan 31 lands on Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30 and so on.
2. **CSV import (`js/csv.js`)**: the file was being cut into lines before quotes were read, so a line break inside a quoted description broke the row. The parser now reads the whole text at once, so quoted fields can contain line breaks (both `\n` and `\r\n`).
3. **Delete after search or sort (`js/app.js`)**: Delete was using the row's position in the filtered or sorted list rather than its position in the full list. It now removes the transaction you clicked.
4. **Refunds in budgets (`js/budget.js`)**: "spent" was adding up every amount regardless of sign. Now only negative amounts (expenses) count, so a refund is ignored.
5. **Balance**: always shown with two decimals (`749.50`).
6. **Reload on `#/budgets` or `#/reports`**: the app ignored the address and always opened the transactions view on load. It now opens the view in the current address, and still defaults to transactions.

**Features**
- **A. Edit**: each row now has an Edit button (class `edit`) next to Delete. Clicking it fills the date, description, amount and category, sets repeat to "none", changes the `#add` label to "Save" and shows `#cancel-edit`. Saving replaces that transaction, so the row count stays the same, and the edit can be undone with `#undo`.
  - `#cancel-edit` leaves edit mode without changing any transaction. It also clears the form fields — I chose that, since the request didn't specify it.
  - Delete, Undo, Redo, Import and Rename also end edit mode, so a save can't land on the wrong row after the list changes.
- **B. Rename**: the budgets view has a new row with `#rename-from`, `#rename-to` and `#rename`. It renames every transaction and budget whose category exactly matches the old name. One `#undo` restores the transactions' old category names; budgets aren't part of the undo history, so their new names stay.
- **C. Report**: each `#report` row now has a third column with the change from the previous month (`+12.50`, `-20.00`, or `0.00`). Categories that only had transactions last month get a row with a total of `0.00`.

All existing ids, classes and module exports are unchanged.
